title: Daily Program Hours Recorded for Work Conditioning and Work Hardening
content:
# Daily program hours recorded

**Clause.** A program day in an hour-billed program of the Workers' Compensation Referral — the Work Conditioning Program or the Work Hardening Program — is recorded at the program's maximum daily program hours, as whole hours.

**Order of working.** The recorded program hours of the day are worked out in this order: first the graded phase hours are fixed, then the make-up hours and the re-test hours are added to them, then the re-conditioning cut and the modified-duty shortening are taken off, and the total is never below zero and never above the program's maximum daily program hours, a day that works out below the program's minimum daily program hours being recorded at the hours worked out, which are the hours delivered.

## Reading the clause

- **Unit** — whole hours.
- **Ceiling** — the program's maximum daily program hours; no day is recorded above it.
- **Floor** — zero; no day is recorded below it.
- **Below the daily minimum** — a day that works out below the program's minimum daily program hours is not raised to the minimum; it is recorded at the hours worked out, which are the hours delivered.

## Worked figures

- A program day in a program whose maximum daily program hours are, hypothetically, 8 is recorded at 8 hours.
- A program day in a program whose maximum daily program hours are, hypothetically, 4 is recorded at 4 hours.

## The ceiling and the floor (hypothetical totals)

| Program maximum daily hours | Program minimum daily hours | Total worked out | Hours recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 4 | 10 | 8 — held at the ceiling |
| 8 | 4 | 3 | 3 — below the minimum, recorded as worked out |
| 4 | 2 | a figure below zero | 0 — held at the floor |
